title: Option contracts and protected acceptance periods
shortTitle: Option contracts and protected acceptance periods
summary: An option contract protects an offeree’s opportunity to accept an offer by limiting the offeror’s power to revoke it. It is distinct from acceptance of the underlying transaction.
notes:
The course presents several routes to irrevocability: consideration for a promise to keep an offer open, a statutory firm offer, beginning invited performance under § 45, and qualifying reliance. Drennan illustrates the last route. A stated deadline alone may define when an offer expires without making it irrevocable beforehand. Ask why the offer is protected, for how long, and whether the offeree has actually exercised the option.

The text organizes four routes: a supported promise to keep open, a merchant firm offer under Article 2, beginning invited performance under § 45, and reliance associated with § 87(2). Each has different predicates. The bargain’s terms, the holding-open commitment, acceptance of the underlying offer, and damages following later breach should be analyzed separately. An ordinary offer’s death or rejection rules should not automatically be transferred to an option.
